title: The corpus
description: Works, the pillars they feed, and the events that threatened them. A work is an economic entity with unusual physics -- non-rival, excludable only by forgetting, and perishable. See docs/05-knowledge-economy.md.

year.description: Negative is BCE. No year zero.

arc.description: How the pillar changes form across six thousand years without ever completing.

kind.description: Mechanically distinct. destruction annihilates carriers; displacement moves them somewhere unreachable (the late-game repatriation loop); neglect is not an event at all but the permanent ~300-year palm-leaf recopying drain, which costs more than every raid combined.

tradition.description: vedic, buddhist, jain, epic, story, shastra, tamil, kavya, bhakti, sikh, persianate, folk, modern.

attribution_kind.description: Most of the corpus is attributed rather than authored. That distinction is content, not a data-quality problem.

derives_from.description: The IP graph. Prestige flows backward along these edges, so patronising a foundational work still pays centuries later. Must be acyclic, and a source may not postdate the work deriving from it -- both enforced by tools/build-corpus.mjs.

pillars.description: Which development pillars this work feeds. How knowledge drives development rather than sitting beside it.

survival.description: recension = the original is gone but adaptations survive (Brihatkatha, Panchatantra). This is the redundancy mechanic, historically attested.
